verdict: OK to lend in Pithampur auto OEM — but only to tier-1/tier-2 suppliers with confirmed OEM orders and clean receivables; avoid single-OEM, EV-only and greenfield bets until MP GST turns positive.
title: Pithampur cars & commercial vehicles (OEM): a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Pithampur is a vehicle-assembly and component town: metal, plastics and electronics go in, finished vehicles and sub-assemblies come out, and cash comes back only after the OEM pays.** The OEM holds pricing power; the supplier absorbs commodity swings and carries the working-capital cycle. So when a proposal lands, check who the end customer is and what share of the borrower's sales that one OEM takes; if it is above half, ask for the purchase-order pipeline and the OEM's payment history.

## What the numbers say now
**National output is strong — IIP for NIC 29 is +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D] — but bank credit to the sector is running ahead at +27.0% YoY, a +7.8 pp gap [D].** That gap is where over-lending hides. Locally, Madhya Pradesh GST is -0.1% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, 6.2 pp slower [D] — a real local stress signal. Peer results are healthy: M&M automotive revenue +25% with EBIT margin 9.5% [5], Tata Motors CV net profit ₹2,560 crore on volumes +26% [6], and Q4FY26 auto EBITDA growth seen at about 21% [4]. But peers also flag margin pressure from commodity and freight costs [4][7]. Note [4] and [5] are April–May 2026 and [6] is dated 12 Aug 2026 — treat them as recent history, not current quarter.

## Where the growth is
**The live local news is capacity, not demand: EKA Mobility has inaugurated six facilities across Pune and Pithampur for electric commercial vehicles, components and interiors [1][2], and Classic Legends' Pithampur plant is near full utilisation with a greenfield under evaluation [3].** Pursue tier-1 and tier-2 suppliers with confirmed orders from these plants, tooling and interior vendors, and established ICE component makers adding an EV line. Avoid pure-play EV startups with no production history, and single-customer borrowers whose only order is a new plant's ramp-up.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the receivable, not the optimism: bill-discounting and invoice-backed limits tied to the OEM's acceptance, with a debtor cap per OEM.** Take monthly stock-and-debtor statements, monthly sales register, and quarterly GSTR-2B versus purchase register. Covenant a minimum interest cover and a cap on total debt to tangible net worth, per ICRA's auto-component methodology [10]. For any greenfield or expansion request, ask for land and plant approvals and the customer's letter of intent before sanction.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the borrower's receivable days against the OEM's stated payment terms, and the local GST number.** If MP GST stays negative while the borrower reports rising sales, ask for e-way bills. If a single OEM's share crosses the agreed cap, cut the limit. If commodity inflation forces OEM price hikes [6], check whether the borrower can pass it on — if not, reprice.

Monthly GST returns and e-way bill data
MP GST stays negative while borrower sales rise -> ask for invoices and reconcile
Inventory days rise with flat sales -> reduce drawing power
Monthly bank statement of the borrower
Cheque returns or delayed OEM receipts -> move to invoice-backed limits only
